grand_strategy.reading:
Bhutan runs the strategy of a small state that has bought its security by
tying it to one neighbour and then spent the proceeds on its own autonomy:
the 2007 treaty removed the clause that made Thimphu take India's advice, but
the hydropower grid, the rupee peg and the Indian grants keep the arrangement
close to the old one. Its three open fronts are China (no relations, an
undelineated border, Doklam in 2017, villages since 2016 that Thimphu does not
contest in public), the outside world (a deliberately thin network, a
carbon-negative and GNH brand used as the voice in the UN and elsewhere) and its
own population, which is leaving for Australia and beyond. The 2024 election
returned Tshering Tobgay (PDP, 30 of 47 seats according to one report) as prime
minister from late January 2024. The Gelephu Mindfulness City, with its
Indian-funded rail link, is the bet: if it works, Bhutan gets a second economic
base besides hydropower and a new reason for young people to stay. If it does
not, it is one more Indian-built asset. Gaps not covered in this card: Ukraine and
Gaza positions, Thailand and Singapore, the Gulf, and the US 2025 contacts beyond
the 10% tariff.

stances.note: The 2007 Friendship Treaty (signed 8 Feb 2007, in force 2 Mar 2007) replaced the 1949 treaty and removed the clause that Bhutan follow India's advice on external relations; Article 2 bars either side from letting its territory be used against the other. That is a treaty alignment, hence ally. Warming: the 2024 Modi visit with INR 10,000 crore for the 13th Plan, the Punatsangchhu-II completion (2025), the Kokrajhar-Gelephu rail approval (Sept 2025). Friction is structural, not open: Doklam 2017 (India halted the PLA road in June, citing a request from Bhutan and its own security concerns; Bhutan protested the road, India's and China's statements did not name Bhutan). The ngultrum is pegged at par to the rupee. Bond - affinity: no kinship, but sympathy and a long protected-state history, not shared identity.

stances.note: No diplomatic relations, no treaty of friendship, an undelineated border (a 1961 Chinese map altered the traditional line), and Thimphu has an honorary consul in Macau and Hong Kong instead of an embassy. The 1998 agreement on peace and tranquillity in the border areas is the only settled text, and the 2021 roadmap and 2023 joint demarcation team are the current track. Doklam (2017) and the Chinese villages (22 by Barnett's count, eight near Doklam, reported by satellite in Dec 2024) are the friction. Bhutan keeps a disciplined silence and China denies building them. No source calls the relation rival: the grade is our reading of competing claims and frictions with no will to destroy the other (confidence C, per the Kosovo-Serbia precedent). Bond - grievance: the 1950 invasion of Tibet and the border that was never settled.

stances.note: Relations established 1983 and tense since 1992 over the repatriation of Nepali-origin refugees from Bhutan (107,000 in seven camps in south-east Nepal, with resettlement offers from the US for 60,000 and six other countries for 10,000 each). The grade is neutral, not rival: there is no competing interest in play today, only a legacy. Bond - grievance: the expulsions of the 1990s are the open wound. Source is the Wikipedia index only (tier 4); the refugee figures and the 1992 date need a primary source before this stance is raised.

stances.note: Transactional, not aligned. Bhutan was the first country to recognise Bangladeshi independence (1971) and has a resident embassy in Thimphu, one of only three. The cooperation on the table is hydropower through India: the trilateral MoU with Bangladesh and India (Dorjilung, 1,024 MW in one version) was reported as endorsed by Bhutan and Bangladesh while India's consent was still awaited, and the Bhutanese ambassador in Dhaka described it as still in discussion. No signed deal found. Bond - affinity: shared SAARC and BIMSTEC membership and the 1971 recognition, not kinship. Sources are the Wikipedia index (tier 4) and one undated Bhutanese report, hence C.

stances.note: No diplomatic relations; the two sides describe warm informal relations and consular ties, and the US embassy in New Delhi is accredited to Bhutan (Wikipedia index). The 2025 contact found is the 10% baseline tariff on Bhutanese exports, which an ADB economist put at about 0.1% of GDP; Thimphu imposed no counter-tariff. Dated to 2025 because that is the first dated action in our sources; the relation itself has no start date in them. Neutral because there is no significant posture, rather than partner, since no transactional arrangement exists. Bond - none: pure interest, nothing underneath. US resettlement of Nepali-origin refugees (1990s-2000s) is the historic tie, not a current one. The US 2025 contacts beyond the tariff were not found.

stances_toward.note: Rival on competing claims, not on hostility. Beijing's MFA does not use the word: its joint release on the 15th Expert Group Meeting (Beijing, 30 Mar-1 Apr 2026) speaks of 'candid, constructive talks' on the Three-Step Road-map, of keeping the negotiations moving and of a joint technical team on the areas without dispute. The grade is the structure behind the talks: about 295 square miles (764 sq km) in the north and west, Doklam and three other areas, are disputed by both sides, the cross-border villages near Doklam are the friction, and there are no diplomatic relations to settle it through. Not adversary: Beijing wants a settled line, not Bhutan's end. Stable: the talks move at their own pace while the villages stay. Bond none: Beijing holds no kinship and no grievance here; the 1950 wound in Thimphu's card is Thimphu's, not Beijing's. Confidence C: the reading is ours, and the MFA release is tier 1 for the process only.
